original_value: Diseases from Ginkgo biloba have brought great losses to medicine and the economy. Therefore, if the degree of disease can be automatically identified in Ginkgo biloba leaves, people will take appropriate measures to avoid losses in advance. Deep learning has made great achievements in plant disease identification and classification. For this paper, the convolution neural network model was used to classify the different degrees of ginkgo leaf disease. This study used the VGGNet-16 and Inception V3 models. After preprocessing and training 1322 original images under laboratory conditions and 2408 original images under field conditions, 98.44% accuracy was achieved under laboratory conditions and 92.19% under field conditions with the VGG model. The Inception V3 model achieved 92.3% accuracy under laboratory conditions and 93.2% under field conditions. Thus, the Inception V3 model structure was more suitable for field conditions. To our knowledge, there is very little research on the classification of different degrees of the same plant disease. The success of this study will have a significant impact on the prediction and early prevention of ginkgo leaf blight.

result.paraphrase: Ginkgo biloba diseases have caused major losses in both medicine and the economy. Therefore, automatically identifying the severity of disease in Ginkgo biloba leaves would allow people to take timely measures and prevent losses in advance. Deep learning has achieved major progress in plant disease identification and classification. In this paper, a convolutional neural network was used to classify different severity levels of ginkgo leaf disease. The study employed VGGNet-16 and Inception V3 models. After preprocessing and training 1322 original images under laboratory conditions and 2408 original images under field conditions, the VGG model reached 98.44% accuracy in the lab and 92.19% in the field. The Inception V3 model achieved 92.3% accuracy under laboratory conditions and 93.2% under field conditions. As a result, the Inception V3 architecture was better suited to field conditions. To our knowledge, there has been very little research on classifying different degrees of the same plant disease. The success of this study will have a significant impact on predicting and preventing ginkgo leaf blight early.
